story_review.one_viewing_summary: Observed in the timed muted strips. A tower camera's display pans dry land and pulls back to the tower. 16 of 56 cameras light as sixteen is heard. Smoke appears on open land in the display and is flagged on smoke. The alert card goes to the crew truck and lands on its dash phone at AEP Texas team. The dash clock marks an estimated window of up to ten minutes. In the display the plume keeps burning and the cameras don't stop fires. A dashed line from the truck stops short of a responder badge on can share. The utility's wildfire lead reports no major fire since launch over the visor calendar. The response record stays blank. The plan waits on state approval.
story_review.opening_to_ending: Opens on what the camera sees and ends on the alert landed with the crew, the line to responders open and the plan awaiting approval.
story_review.weakest_transition: s4-shot-2 to s5-shot-1: from the dash clock in the cab straight back into the lens display with no physical bridge.

subject_recognition.observed: A white camera head sits on a lattice tower top beside a large round display whose picture of red land and horizon pans as the head turns. From 2.79 s the view pulls back to the whole tall tower and its beam over the plains with a windmill, a pumpjack and a white pickup.

contact_and_consequence.observed: The ALERT card slides out of the display's lower edge, runs low to the parked truck from 14.5 to 15.0 s, then in the cab comes in at the windshield and lands on the dash-mounted phone as a bubble that stays visible from 16.5 to 17.5 s.

dominant_action.observed: The display's own picture pans onto smoke rising from open land and the flag box closes and locks on it by 13.5 s, then the card performs the send from the display to the truck and onto the phone. The labels only follow the actions.

surface_finish.observed: The cab reads as finished authored art with roof liner, pillars, visors, mirror, dash, wheel, the dash phone and a black dash clock whose hatched orange window opens. The weakest finish is the undersized station in s5.

continuity.observed: The display and head pull back to the same tower. The display that flags the smoke sends the card to the truck and that truck's cab carries the phone, clock and visor calendar. The display returns at 22.78 s, the tower, truck and station share the s5 wide, and the display, truck and station return in the closing. Every frame carries the Illustration disclosure.

closing_payoff.observed: The top band shows the Wildfire plan folder, Filed August 24th, an open State approval slot and an outlined Expected January 2027 tag. Below, the display still shows the burning plume, the truck carries the landed alert and a short dashed line stops before the station badge.

first_frame.observed: Frame one is the camera head and its round display already panning land, so the subject and its watching action are visible immediately.

visual_progression.observed: Display, tower pull-back, lens slots lighting, planned slots and tag, smoke flagged in the display, card to the truck, cab phone, dash clock window and tag, display hold with tag, open-line wide, visor calendar and attribution, tailgate record, desk and composite: each shot adds a new state.

shot_variety.observed: Close display, wide pull-back, medium card, close plan card, medium display, close card exit, medium cab, close clock and closer tag, medium display hold, wide s5, medium and detail calendar, close and detail record, close desk and a split composite.

performed_turn.observed: A dashed line runs low from the truck's landed alert toward the station badge, stops short with an open ring, and Can share pins at about 27.0 s as can share is heard. It is small and the tag covers the station roof.

pace.observed: A new visible change arrives at least every 4 s on the measured clock and no shot runs past 4.32 s. The weakest stretch is 29.26 to 32.52 s where the small visor calendar barely changes.

closing_answer.observed: The alert is landed with the crew, the line to responders stays open and the plan waits on state approval in one frame, with no invented outcome.

finished_art.observed: The bezelled display with its compass tape, the panning land with smoke and flag box, the cab, phone and clock read as finished authored art. The s5 station scale is the weakest finish.
